Such a meaning would, of course, be ludicrous for the tentative first step in this article.
The ordering of the perceptual tasks does not provide a complete prescription for how to make a graph. Rather, it provides a set of guidelines that must be used with judgment in designing a graph.
We cannot realistically claim to have isolated 10 basic, independent perceptual tasks. Each task is really a complex set of tasks, and there is much overlap.
We have no proof that our laboratory results are realistic and work in the field, but it appears plausible that this is so.
